bibl.title: Kalila wa Dimna Manuscript
bibl.note: Arabic manuscript witness for textual comparison.

body.p: When the cat saw him, he sensed perdition.

p.n: The Rat Resolves to Cut the Last Rope

body.p:
So the rat said to the cat,
‘now is the place for diligence in cutting what remains of your cords.’”

“Before the huntsman came close,
the rat had finished cutting the cords, despite the cat’s mistrust and his perplexity.”

p.n: The Cat and the Rat Escape

body.p:
“When he finished,
the cat ran to the tree and climbed it, the rat dived into
his burrow], and the huntsman grabbed his shredded cords and net and left feeling disappointed.”

p.n: The Cat Calls Back the Rat

body.p:
The rat came out
of his burrow after that, saw the cat from afar and dreaded approaching him.
‘O, friend,’ therefore cried the cat, ‘you who have done me a good deed What

p.n: The Cat Reminds the Rat of their Friendship

body.p:
is stopping you from approaching me, so that I can endow you with the best for the favor you have done me Do come to me
and don’t sever my brotherly ties;

p.n: If One Gives Up a Friend One Loses Out

body.p:
for he who takes a friend and cuts off any brotherly connections
will be prevented from reaping the fruits of friendship and brotherhood, and brethren and friends will despair from obtaining benefits from him.
Your favor to me cannot be forgotten, and you are entitled to seek the reward
